key_findings.detail:
Standard accelerated PID testing applies **−1000 V** DC bias between the shorted cell terminals and the module frame, based on IEC 62804 protocols. However, degradation has been observed at much lower voltages:

- Minimal PID degradation occurs below **200 V**; significant degradation appears above **400 V**; drastic degradation at **1000 V** and above.
- [[papers/Elsevier-541-3483-2-s2.0-84991699729-2016-J-Microscopic aspects of potential induced degradation phenomena and their recovery processes for p ty.pdf#page=1|Luo et al. (2016), p.1]]

PID is strongly polarity-dependent. Negative bias on the cell (relative to the frame) drives Na⁺ ions from the front glass toward the cell. Positive bias reverses or suppresses this migration:

- Complete PID suppression observed when a positive voltage (+1000 V) was applied at 85°C, compared to essentially no suppression at +1000 V and 25°C.
- [[papers/IOP-53-3675-2-s2.0-84956692262-2016-J-Consideration on Na diffusion and recovery phenomena in potential-induced degradation for crystallin.pdf#page=1|Masuda et al. (2016), p.1]]

In TOPCon modules, no degradation was observed on the rear face in either polarity, and no degradation on the front face with positive voltage:
- [[papers/Wiley-105-888-2-s2.0-85183130481-2024-J-Field-representative evaluation of PID-polarization in TOPCon PV modules by accelerated stress testi.pdf#page=1|Luo et al. (2024), p.1]]

The applied system voltage creates an electric field of approximately **0.5–1 MV/cm** across the 80–200 nm SiNx antireflective coating (ARC). This field:

- Reduces Na⁺ transit time through 80 nm PECVD SiNx from ~1 million years (diffusion only) to **~25 minutes** at 80°C with $0.5$ MV/cm applied field.
- [[papers/Elsevier-564-3774-2-s2.0-84940452054-2015-J-Drift characteristics of mobile ions in SiNx films and solar cells.pdf#page=2|Wilson et al. (2015), p.2]]

The system voltage drives a leakage current through the path: Al frame → glass surface → encapsulant bulk → cell ARC. This current carries ionic charge (primarily Na⁺) to the cell surface:

- A one-to-one quantitative relationship was established between **charge transferred onto the active cell area** and **power loss**, demonstrating that accumulated ionic dose directly controls degradation magnitude.
- [[papers/IOP-44-3195-2-s2.0-85039161903-2017-J-Quantitative analysis of relationship between leakage current and power loss of multi-crystalline si.pdf#page=1|Kawamura et al. (2017), p.1]]

For CIGS modules, a negative bias causes alkali metal cations (Na⁺ from soda-lime glass substrate) to drift through the Mo back contact into the CIGS absorber. Borosilicate glass substrates (with K⁺ instead of Na⁺) show **35× lower leakage current** and dramatically reduced degradation due to lower K⁺ mobility:
- [[papers/IEEE-267-2998-2-s2.0-85051002389-2018-J-Potential-Induced Degradation of Cu(In,Ga)Se2 Solar Cells: Alkali Metal Drift and Diffusion Effects.pdf#page=1|Theelen et al. (2018), p.1]]

For perovskite cells, negative bias at 1000 V causes complete failure in the majority of cells (7/8 cells) within 1000 hours:
- [[papers/Wiley-190-1756-2-s2.0-85121464246-2022-J-Are Perovskite Solar Cell Potential-Induced Degradation Proof?.pdf#page=2|Brecl et al. (2022), p.2]]
